main_text.p: Quod posterius moribus suis illaudatis ipsi debuêre. Fuisse enim Ætolos accepimus feroces, jactabundos, supra modum arrogantes, ingratos, invidos,iniquos, avaros, alieni cupidos, sui prodigos, rapto vivere suetos,turbulentos, saltuosos, amicis infidos, inconstantes, quietis & æqui juris impatientissimos, temerarios, irâ præcipites, propositi pertinaces. Ità factum, ut multos sæpe offenderent, suam & aliorum quietem turbarent. Ut priora omittam, cum injuriis lacessivissent vicinos,& vicissim armis Macedonum aliorumque premerentur, extremum discrimen auxilio Achæorum adjuti evasere. Non multò post cum viderent potentia & gloria crescere Achæos, malevolentiâ stimulati exitiale fœdus inter Cleomenem regem Spartanum & Antigonum Macedoniam tutorio nomine pro Philippo puero rege gubernantem in perniciem Achæorum conflarunt, & simul discordiâ distrahere eosdem Achæos studuerunt. Sed prudentiâ Arati, qui Antigonum obliquâ oratione percommodè in partes Achæorum traxit, consilium hoc eorum nequissimum in exitium Cleomenis, Achæorum hostis infestissimi, & in ipsorum autorum dolorem ac infamiam, in suorum verò r[illegible, ~6 letters]

page.notes: The scan is cut off at the foot of the page; the last word of the text is illegible and continues below, where only "xim" is partly visible under a stamp. Stamps and show-through at the lower right and left margin are not transcribed. The left margin has decorative strokes and binding marks, not printed notes. No marginal notes are printed. Long s was rendered as s throughout, including "saltuosos", "vicissim" and "stimulati". Printed spellings such as "debuêre", "invidos,iniquos" and "vicinos,& vicissim" are kept as printed.
